title: Ukraine blew up Putin’s bridge using relay drones to bypass Starlink limits
author: Jeremy Hsu
body: A Ukrainian barrage of missiles and drones collapsed a crucial segment of Russian President Vladimir Putin’s prized Kerch Strait Bridge—and Ukraine’s military pulled off the strike deep within Russian-occupied territory without relying on the military-grade version of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite communications to guide the missiles in. On the nights of November 15 and November 16, coordinated waves of Ukrainian drones and missiles caused enough damage to collapse one of two steel arches supporting the Kerch bridge’s roadway for automobile traffic, according to an Institute for the Study of War update . Russian sources claimed several hundred Ukrainian drones first overwhelmed Russian air defenses to pave the way for remote-controlled missile strikes focused on the bridge, with the latter prominently including Ukraine’s homegrown Flamingo cruise missile. The Ukrainian operation adapted a Russian battlefield innovation by using drones equipped with mesh radios to create an airborne communications network, according to the Financial Times . Each networked drone acts as a relay node to extend the communication link between human operators and remotely piloted missiles and strike drones. Russia began using the technique to support long-range drone and missile strikes on Ukrainian cities. Read full article Comments

title: Meet the NPCs of Vice City: How characters react to players
body: On a walk through Vice City, you might pass tourists taking vacation photos, someone playing Frisbee with their dog, or a bouncer working the door at a club. A little farther down the street, you could see a carjacking, a police chase, or someone dancing on the roof of a car. And all of that can happen while you're just on your way to buy a T-shirt or pair of shoes. Ahead of Grand Theft Auto VI s Nov. 19 release on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S , early reviews, gameplay clips, and livestreamers are giving us a better sense of who we'll meet in Vice City and across Leonida, Rockstar's fictional version of Florida. The game is packed full of NPCs, short for non-player characters , and stopping to talk to one can lead to anything from a quick hello to a whole new side quest. The detail that went into many of these characters is clearly impressive, or as one X user said, " nothing short of magic ," which makes sense considering Rockstar put together an entire team in Los Angeles to give the people you pass on the street more personality. title: Trump abandons his FDA nominee, and Senate scraps vote on his NSF pick
author: Beth Mole
body: In the span of less than 24 hours, two Trump administration nominees have suffered sudden blows—Trump's pick to lead the Food and Drug Administration and his pick to lead the National Science Foundation. Late Tuesday evening, Axios reported that the White House had abruptly withdrawn its controversial nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the FDA. Overton, a top conservative domestic policy aide in the White House, has drawn criticism and skepticism from Republicans and Democrats alike over her stances on vaccines, abortion, vapes, and birth control. Overton opposes abortion—though perhaps not strongly enough for some Republicans—and supported Trump and Kennedy's decried anti-vaccine policies and statements, vexing Democrats. In her confirmation hearing in September, Overton consistently stonewalled senators on every topic, refusing to directly answer even softball questions from friendly Republicans, leaving lawmakers on both sides of the aisle openly frustrated. The questions she dodged included those on how she would handle the FDA's current safety review of the abortion pill, mifepristone, which extensive data has established is extremely safe. She also wouldn't say whether she agreed with Trump when he falsely claimed the measles vaccine is "quite lethal" or that children are given vaccine doses the "size of a soda bottle." Overton repeatedly refused to answer whether Trump could ever be wrong. Read full article Comments

title: Windows Server 2028 trades compatibility for out-of-the-box security
author: Nick Indge
body: Microsoft's Ignite announcements this week went beyond the Office-in-Copilot overhaul with the reveal of the Windows Server 2028 Public Preview and its new security-by-default stance and what Microsoft calls Hardened Server Core . Windows Server 2028 will implement a default security framework that Microsoft says is aligned with hardened DoD benchmarks, such as the Defense Information Systems Agency's (DISA) Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG). STIGs work by providing a standard security framework for system administrators to follow recommended guidance. In the past, Windows Server admins were left to start from a blank canvas and then implement hardening configurations for operations. Secure baselines were available but not the default. Microsoft says that concern is now managed: "The s ecure configuration is the starting state, not a project you run after setup. That closes the window where a newly deployed server sits exposed while it waits to be hardened. " The new Windows Server 2028 hardened-by-default state will only be available for the Server Core installs. Windows Server Desktop Experience installs do not include the changed stance. Read full article Comments

body: Scattered Spider was once called "one of the most dangerous financial criminal groups" by Microsoft cybersecurity researchers. The U.S. has now closed the case against five of the group's members, sending the final defendant to prison for more than half a decade. British Scattered Spider member Tyler Robert Buchanan has just been sentenced to six years in prison, according to the DOJ. Buchanan, who is 24 years old, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud and aggravated identity theft. SEE ALSO: What is 'Scattered Spider'? How this massive phishing scam worked. The five Scattered Spider hackers took part in a massive phishing campaign which targeted employees of major technology companies, telecommunications companies, and entertainment companies between September 2021 and April 2023. During this time, Scattered Spider carried out a massive phishing scheme where they posed as employers or their IT providers, spamming employees with text messages that urged them to log in to phishing websites. Once the victims logged in, Scattered Spider hackers weaponized these stolen credentials in order to access employees' accounts and their employers' computer systems. The hackers took confidential business information and individuals' credentials and private data. Using this information, Scattered Spider also deployed SIM-swapping attacks which resulted in the hackers stealing at least $11.6 million from cryptocurrency wallets. title: The "shameful" measles data that lost the US its elimination status
author: Beth Mole
body: International health authorities formally announced on Tuesday that the US has lost its measles elimination status, a hard-fought public health triumph won in 2000 after decades-long vaccination efforts. The loss had been widely expected by public health experts for months, and the decision was leaked by the press last week. Still, having the designation officially stripped stings. After the announcement Tuesday, public health experts, doctors, and political leaders decried the dramatic backslide for the US, calling it " shameful " and a " national embarrassment ." News articles point to the staggering vertical rise of measles cases this year, currently over 5,400 cases , more than any other year since 1991. An explosive measles outbreak in Pennsylvania accounts for over 1,500 of those cases . There have been 10 confirmed deaths across three states, several deaths just in the last week. But the measles data that caused the US to lose its status—the bits of it that are public at least—paint a darker picture of where the US is in its rematch with measles, the most contagious virus known on Earth. For one thing, almost none of the data from this year—the cases, the explosive Pennsylvania outbreak, the deaths—factored in to the loss. It was lost earlier. What's happening now is a runaway epidemic. Read full article Comments

title: The future of tech will not be inclusive by default
body: Ten years ago, QueerTech began with a feeling that too many 2SLGBTQI+ people in the technology sector know well: not belonging. My co-founder Andy Salda a and I were working at different companies in tech and kept running into the same frustration. We could see the possibility of the sector around us, had the skills to succeed, and believed technology, when stewarded responsibly, could change lives. Yet we could not see a place for ourselves, as queer professionals, within it. I grew up in Morocco, where being queer was, and continues to be, illegal. In 2007, I left for New York City in pursuit of the "American Dream." There, I quickly realized this dream was based on a contradiction opportunity without equal rights. Finally, I moved to Montreal, drawn to Canada s reputation for respecting people across cultures, religions, and identities. SEE ALSO: Meta is allegedly deleting LGBTQ and plus-sized business Instagram accounts Across this journey, I expected geography to change my sense of belonging. It never did. So in 2016, Andy and I started small. QueerTech was a volunteer-run community group built around a simple need: to find one another, create connections, and make space for queer people in an industry where many of us felt invisible. Now, well over 15 years later, Wright is starting to promote his next digital simulation, which will use generative AI technology to craft a game-like experience from players' memories. MyMems , which is slated to release next year, differentiates itself from Wright's previous projects by "turn[ing] the simulation inward," as Wright's Gallium Studios and partner Artificial Agency put it in a press release this morning . The game will mine memories provided by the player to create digital people that can then form teams to solve puzzles in the game world. “If my Grandmother ended up in a Grand Slam match against Serena Williams, who would win?" title: YouTube will now guess how many people are co-viewing on TV
body: YouTube is making another big change to how views are counted on long-form videos, YouTube Shorts, and livestreams. According to a company update , YouTube will now include "co-views" in public video view counts. What is a co-view? It's YouTube's estimate of how many people are watching content together on TV via a single account. YouTube says it will include these estimated views because "viewers are now watching over 1 billion hours of YouTube on TVs every day." The company says it wants to "credit creators true reach" and "provide a more complete picture of how audiences are engaging with content." SEE ALSO: Is YouTube getting a separate social networking app? This isn't the first recent change to how YouTube counts video views. This past summer, the platform started counting views from the moment a video plays. Previously, viewers had to watch for a specific amount of time, typically around 30 seconds for long-form videos, in order for their view to be counted in the public metric. Co-views is certainly a bit more offbeat than that, as the company is essentially inflating view counts by estimating how many people are watching together on a single device that would've previously been counted as a single view. YouTube, however, says this new platform metric "aligns with TV industry standards, including how traditional broadcast and streaming networks estimate the total number of people exposed to content." title: Waymo has stopped its robotaxis from driving on the freeway—here’s why
author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
body: Waymo is currently restricting its fleet of robotaxis to surface streets after getting into hot water with California over its cars' driving behavior on highways. Specifically, the software tends to drive into construction zones at speed. As first reported by the San Francisco Business Times , this behavior actually drew the ire of California’s DMV earlier this month, which ordered Waymo to stop driving on Californian highways immediately and until it can convince the DMV that its cars no longer “pose an imminent hazard to public safety.” This is not Waymo’s first run-in with this problem. In Arizona, Waymo robotaxis did not recognize ramp closure signs on six occasions in Phoenix in April and entered construction zones. A month later in California, seven Waymo robotaxis entered lanes with active construction. In June, Waymo recalled the almost 3,800 robotaxis capable of highway driving. That problem led Waymo to stick to surface streets only in California after the May incidents until late July, when the robotaxis resumed highway operations. In early July, Waymo told the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration that it began updating the robotaxi software to a version that “improve[s] the recognition of freeway construction zones, more appropriately prioritize[s] construction zones over other freeway hazards, and reduce[s] speed when the AV detects that it may be in a construction zone.” Read full article Comments

Beginning Dec. 11, The Odyssey will once again be available in the premium formats it was specifically designed for. Nolan's critically heralded hit is the first feature shot entirely with IMAX film cameras, so the only way to see all of the frame is by catching it in IMAX 70mm, with its square-like 1.43:1 aspect ratio. Standard IMAX is the next biggest option, with a 1.90:1 aspect ratio. The distinction between viewing formats turned IMAX 70mm tickets into a hot commodity this summer, with people spending hundreds of dollars and even undertaking international trips for the chance to see The Odyssey. SEE ALSO: 'The Odyssey' has made IMAX 70mm a status symbol The IMAX re-release news comes one day after The Odyssey became available on digital . While Nolan's reverence for large-scale formats and theatrical experiences has sparked memes like " watching the way Nolan intended, " the Academy Award-winning director expressed enthusiasm for people to catch the film at home, and yes, that includes on their phones. "In the course of my lifetime, the way we're able to engage with movies at home has gone forward leaps and bounds from VHS to DVD to streaming at 4K. Report (Data, Advice, Trends, and Expertise), called Dating While Dreaming Big, Hinge found some hope in daters. Gen Z singles are seeing possibility in their future partners and how they can lead to their ideal future selves. title: How The Verge is picking which Black Friday deals to share
body: For the past month, we’ve been inundated with Black Friday deals, signaling what’s to come on the biggest shopping day of the year in the US. We routinely get dozens of press releases a day, coming from brands big and small that hope that we’ll publicize these offers. Of course, the companies would prefer that we don’t do any research on these deals to see if they’re actually good, and most don’t provide any of the necessary context we’re looking for when vetting them. Most indicators of a good deal are confusing — not just for us, but for anyone who’s shopping. Groundwork Collaborative recently published its findings about the unclear manner in which Amazon displays deals. Its researchers tracked a selection of products ahead of Black Friday and Cyber Monday in 2024 and 2025, and they claim that nearly one in three products advertised as deals on Amazon didn’t offer savings during the actual shopping events. The investigation also found that nearly a tenth of the deals it examined were more expensive during the sales events than on some days in the month leading up to them. Something we commonly see on Amazon and attempt to correct for in our coverage are good deals with inflated discount claims. As in, the original retail amount (the “list” price) is sometimes higher than the usual day-to-day price to make the savings seem more substantial. Sometimes, the manufacturer’s suggested retail price (MSRP) is what’s shown, though that’s not always the case. title: Voyager 1 at one light-day: Historian revisits Golden Record's forgotten details
author: Robert Pearlman
body: In the one light-day that humanity's most distant object has now traveled from Earth, there has been enough time for details about its creation—and what it left behind—to be discovered again. Voyager 1, which left Earth in 1977 on an initial mission to fly by Jupiter and Saturn (as well as the latter's moon Titan), crossed into interstellar space in 2012. Like its twin (Voyager 2), Voyager 1 carries a "commemorative phonograph record," in part as a nod to the 100th anniversary of the recording medium and as a message from humanity to whoever (or whatever) encounters the spacecraft on its journey through outer space. About those forgotten bits, ask Glen Swanson . While researching the history of the Golden Record, he uncovered the discs' overlooked second set of operating directions and located the duplicates that were made and distributed almost five decades ago. title: GTA 6 is the highest-rated game of all time
body: Grand Theft Auto VI is officially out and critics love it . title: Grand Theft Auto VI: The Ars Technica review
author: Kyle Orland
body: Just a minute ago, I was shooting my way out of a cocaine deal gone wrong, darting behind furniture for cover. Now I’m sitting on the floor of my home, working through the instructions to construct an Ikea-style coffee table with my partner. A tiny heart with a plus sign pops up, showing that our relationship is stronger for this quotidian domestic effort. This is the contrast at the heart of Grand Theft Auto VI , a game that seems to revel in both action movie bombast and the mundanities of everyday life for an up-and-coming young criminal couple. The reimagined and expanded Vice City is still the grand, crude, satirical criminal playground you’d expect after 25 years of 3D Grand Theft Auto games. And that world is as full, detailed, technically impressive, and polished as you would expect after this latest installment received a reported billion-dollar budget and roughly a decade of development work involving thousands of Rockstar staffers. title: Nvidia ends Jensen Huangs hopes for return as CEO
body: Nvidia held its Q3 2027 earnings call on Tuesday, less than a week after former CEO Jensen Huang resigned amidst reports he had engaged in multiple extramarital affairs including with an alleged Chinese spy . While Huang did not appear during the earnings call, he did publish a statement saying that he would happily return to his former role as Nvidia's CEO if asked. SEE ALSO: Who could replace Jensen Huang at Nvidia long-term? Here are the top contenders. The AI boom has sparked a significant spike in demand for computer components, leading to increasing profits for chipmakers such as Nvidia. Earlier this year, the company reported $81.6 billion in revenue during Q1 and $96.2 billion in Q2 . This growth has continued in Q4, with Nvidia announcing its quarterly revenue had increased by 20 percent to $115.8 billion. However, the elephant in the room was Huang, whose recent scandal and departure prompted a significant drop in Nvidia's stock . During Tuesday's earnings call, Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones stated that Huang had voluntarily resigned on Nov. 12 "after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms." Nvidia is currently searching for a permanent CEO , with CFO Colette Kress acting in the role in the interim. "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," said Jones. title: Hurdle hints and answers for November 18, 2026
body: If you like playing daily word games like Wordle , then Hurdle is a great game to add to your routine. There are five rounds to the game. The first round sees you trying to guess the word, with correct, misplaced, and incorrect letters shown in each guess. If you guess the correct answer, it'll take you to the next hurdle, providing the answer to the last hurdle as your first guess. This can give you several clues or none, depending on the words. For the final hurdle, every correct answer from previous hurdles is shown, with correct and misplaced letters clearly shown. An important note is that the number of times a letter is highlighted from previous guesses does necessarily indicate the number of times that letter appears in the final hurdle. body: Only Murders in the Building 's Season 6 trailer is here, and the podcasters have well and truly left the building. Renamed Only Murders in London , Hulu 's comedy mystery is headed across the pond for its sixth season, with Charles (Steve Martin), Oliver (Martin Short) , and Mabel ( Selena Gomez ) hoping to discover what happened to their latest true crime podcast subject. title: FAA official oversaw router work just before nationwide ground stop, report claims
body: An official with the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) was on the ground in Arkansas when new telecommunications wires were replaced, an action that preceded Friday's national ground stop by eight minutes, according to the Washington Post . The FAA official oversaw the work, tested it, and signed off on it, according to the Post 's report. The work involved replacing a router and swapping old copper wires for new fiber-optic cables, part of a national effort by the FAA to upgrade the airline industry's communication infrastructure. SEE ALSO: Apple confirms iCloud sign-in issues, App Store and Apple Pay outages The fact that an FAA official greenlit the work complicates Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy's efforts to point fingers at L3Harris Technologies, a tech services provider and contractor tasked with updating the wires in Arkansas and leading the FAA's fiber-optic upgrades. Duffy said on Saturday that his agency is looking into whether "incompetence" by L3Harris led to the 4.5-hour ground stop. Responding to the Post 's request for comment, the FAA pointed to statements Duffy made on Tuesday in a news conference at the Capitol. During the conference, Duffy said that he wanted L3Harris to "hire better minds" for the wire replacement work and was considering bringing in new contractors to help. An exact cause for the communications outage has not yet been confirmed, an anonymous source told the Post . Duffy told reporters on Saturday that the replaced router in Arkansas was faulty and flooded the network with over 1,000 connection attempts every few seconds ,

title: Copilot is "the new OS for work," and now Office runs inside of it
author: Nick Indge
body: Opening the keynote at its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the company's vision for its new "frontier ecosystem," announcing Tuesday the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he described as "the new OS for work." The announcement is a striking inversion of how we've traditionally used software. Rather than an app like Word being the attraction and Clippy the assistant to help you use it, Microsoft envisions the new Copilot integrations will see agents driving things, with the software packages riding shotgun. Applications will become plugin components of the agent's work, backed by an organizational knowledge layer that draws context from emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files. Users will now be able to create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations directly in Copilot, with the resulting files remaining editable in their respective Office applications. body: Autonomous cab giant Waymo has suspended freeway access for its fleet of vehicles following a safety notice from the California Department of Motor Vehicles. SEE ALSO: California sues OpenAI for being a 'public nuisance' Frist reported by the San Francisco Business Times , the California DMV issued a notice on Nov. 11 that a small number of Waymo vehicles in the San Francisco Bay Area had entered restricted construction zones on U.S. Route 101 despite notice of closures. Another vehicle reportedly impeded California Highway Patrol on Highway 280. Because of these "recurring incursions," the state announced it would ban self-driving taxis from state freeways until the company implemented "effective corrective actions," the DMV said in a statement to TechCrunch. The department called the incidents an imminent hazard to public safety. Waymo, which is owned by Google's parent holding company, Alphabet, responded by pausing freeway access for its entire nationwide fleet. Freeways had been accessible to Waymo cabs in select cities since 2025, with a brief, unexplained pause from May to July of this year. "In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance," said Waymo spokesperson Dana Gallagher. "Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. title: Hundreds of websites deliver potent malware cocktail to unsuspecting visitors
author: Dan Goodin
body: Hundreds of websites using the Optimizely website personalization platform served unsuspecting visitors a potent malware cocktail that targeted cryptocurrency wallets, stole payment card data, cookies, and screenshots, and delivered exploit kits for infecting iPhones and iPads, researchers said Tuesday. ReportURI said it identified 178 websites—including CNN, Zoom, the BBC, and Salesforce—that were affected. JavaScript digitally signed by Optimizely and then loaded into customer pages had been modified to include malicious components that attempted to infect visitor devices with multiple payloads. When wares were installed successfully, they swapped user cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the attackers. Other components skimmed payment cards, stole cookies and screenshots, and, on iPhones and iPads, delivered iOS exploit kits known as Coruna and DarkSword. Optimizely infrastructure delivers multipurpose malware Optimizely serves JavaScript “snippets” that include both company code and code that is provided by each customer. The JavaScript, which can be served directly from Optimizely or from a customer endpoint, runs on every page the customer serves. Somehow, the attackers wrote their own code into a portion of each affected customer’s JavaScript and then delivered it from cdn.optimizely.com. A valid certificate for that domain signed the JavaScript. Read full article Comments

title: OpenAI sued by California after admitting to 80 loss-of-control incidents
author: Jon Brodkin
body: California sued OpenAI yesterday, alleging it has tried to evade responsibility for the Hugging Face attack and about 80 other incidents in which the company lost control of its AI. The lawsuit was filed under the state's public nuisance and unfair competition laws. The July 2026 hack of Hugging Face and other attacks carried out by OpenAI's autonomous agents "may just be the tip of the iceberg," said a lawsuit filed in a state court by California Attorney General Rob Bonta. "OpenAI recently admitted to the Attorney General’s Office that it has lost control of its autonomous AI agents over 80 times during testing." OpenAI had publicly reported only 27 such incidents, showing that "OpenAI’s public reports do not represent the full scope of loss-of-control incidents involving OpenAI’s models that have impacted third parties," the lawsuit said. OpenAI "knowingly tested a dangerous product without proper oversight or safety procedures and misled the public about it," Bonta said in a press release . Read full article Comments

The Federal Emergency Management Agency ( FEMA ) and the Federal Communications Commission ( FCC ) are conducting a scheduled test of the national emergency alert system at 2:20 p.m. ET on Tuesday, Nov. 17. And on Monday, a JPMorgan Chase outage sparked reports of a major bank outage (the problem was limited to Chase Bank and not a systemic issue or the result of a cyberattack), followed quickly by a United Airlines outage . None of these outages were directly related to or caused by cyberattackers, but the timing has sparked conspiracy theories and generalized anxiety. SEE ALSO: Trump says he takes 'no responsibility' for nationwide FAA ground stop However, the emergency alert was scheduled long before these outages; the FCC also announced a backup date of Dec. 3, in the event today's test does not occur. title: Google makes it easier to use Gemini without training AI on your data
author: Ryan Whitwam
body: It can be hard to use Google products—or even the Internet itself—without coming into contact with Gemini AI. That is, of course, by design . The more you use Gemini, the more data Google collects to train and improve its generative AI chatbot. The options to limit training on your data have been scant, but Google is finally adding more controls to the Gemini app. The change currently rolling out to Gemini will separate your chat history from training, which allows you to retain basic AI functionality without handing Google quite so much control over your data. Prior to this change, the only way to opt out of contributing your chat contents (including attachments) for training was to turn off your history. That made it impossible to go back and pick up a chat down the road. As the new settings roll out, users will see separate toggles for model training and chat history. The history setting will continue to support an adjustable limit, but you will no longer have to change it to stop Google from training on your Gemini usage. Meanwhile, AI training will be an opt-out situation. You'll need to find the toggle to block Google from using your chats for AI training. It's under Activity in the Gemini settings. You can also access the menu from your Google account under Data and Privacy My Activity Other activity Gemini Apps Activity. Read full article Comments

According to the statement, U.S. agencies opened an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 for "potential export control violations" after noticing suspicious activity. The Department of Commerce requested records from Nvidia regarding sales to Megaspeed in May 2025. (The export of advanced AI chips is highly regulated to protect national security, and Nvidia makes many of the chips that power the U.S. AI industry.) One month later, Nvidia put Megaspeed on its "no sell" list. That same month, U.S. agents and Singaporean law enforcement conducted an in-person investigation at Megaspeed and interviewed Megaspeed CEO Alice Huang. Following this on-site action, the Department of Justice "took the lead role in the criminal investigation of Megaspeed," according to the statement. "While we don t typically comment on ongoing investigations, it is in the public interest to provide the facts and address inaccurate information circulating in public reporting," the joint statement says. title: Grok Bot took unapproved actions, ignored orders to stop, and then denied it
author: Dan Goodin
body: Researchers recently discovered unexpected behavior from Grok Bot, the AI agent platform from Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI. Over five days, Grok bots installed on two separate employee laptops made 31 requests to access data stored in employee calendar, email, Slack, and GitHub accounts. The bots performed the actions even though the employees had never ordered them and continued doing them even after employees instructed them to stop. The bots also denied having taken the actions at all. The behavior was reported Tuesday by NewCore, the maker of a managed gateway product that acts as an intermediary between AI agents and the tools and accounts they are assigned to work with. In some cases, the unapproved access attempts occurred while the laptop with Grok Bot installed had its lid shut, or late at night while the employee was sleeping. None of the unprompted actions were recorded in Grok logs. Without the gateway logs, the employees would have had no idea they occurred. And of course, without the gateway, the unapproved accesses would have succeeded—again without the end user's knowledge. It’s “worse than a bug” Once the employees learned that Grok Bot had tried to check in with accounts without prompting, one of them instructed the agent, four separate times, to stop taking any actions on its own. The agent's reply was: “I won’t set that up, and I’ll stop offering recurring check-ins.” Despite acknowledging the explicit instructions, the Grok Bot made more unapproved access attempts. title: Sunrise on the Reaping review: The biggest and boldest Hunger Games yet
body: Are you looking for a movie to thoroughly wallop you? To leave you emotionally battered, physically exhausted, and full of despair and hope at the same time? Then allow me to prescribe a healthy dose of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping , the sixth film in the Hunger Games series. Based on Suzanne Collins' second prequel novel following The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes , Sunrise on the Reaping once again rewinds the clock on Panem to the 50th Hunger Games, otherwise known as the Second Quarter Quell. These are the biggest Hunger Games yet, with 48 tributes instead of the standard 24. Among them is Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada), future mentor to series protagonists Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark. SEE ALSO: The first 20 minutes of 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' blew me away The question here is not whether Haymitch will survive the games. We know, by virtue of the entire original trilogy, that he does. But before he was the cynical, heavy-drinking, lone wolf victor audiences met in The Hunger Games , he was an optimistic 16-year-old with a caring family, a loving relationship, and a solid community in District 12. So the real question of Sunrise on the Reaping becomes, what broke that young man down so thoroughly? The answer is, unsurprisingly, bleak as all hell. But director Francis Lawrence executes it in thrilling (if occasionally overstuffed) fashion, with a Hunger Games sequence that blows series-high Catching Fire 's own games out of the water, and a dogged focus on the philosophical themes at the core of Collins' work. title: Oura launches Jet Lag Plan, letting users hack their travel
body: Oura Ring users who are always on the go are about to benefit from a feature to combat jet lag. Jet Lag Plan is a new Oura feature that creates a plan to navigate time changes before, during, and after travel. We have all been there with travel. As much fun as the vacation is, if you're dealing with time zone changes, jet lag can totally kill the vibe. You don't want to waste a moment in a new place by taking a nap back at the hotel. Oura wants to help its Oura Ring users combat jet lag with its latest feature. The new feature is built off of a National University of Singapore study that used 1.5 million nights of sleep data from de-identified Oura users. Jet Lag Plan builds a plan designed just for you. It uses your flight itinerary along with your sleep patterns and chronotype to craft a series of recommendations. It produces a personalized schedule around sleep, light exposure, activity, and caffeine for journeys that cross three or more time zones. The feature uses Oura's AI-powered support, Oura Advisor, to adjust the plan as travel changes, in case things don't go as expected. Jet Lag Plan will be available globally to users with Gen 3 or newer hardware on both iOS and Android, as long as users have their language set to English. title: California sues OpenAI for being a public nuisance
body: California is suing OpenAI , accusing ChatGPT 's creator of endangering the public by knowingly developing AI models without appropriate safeguards. It also alleges that the AI company constitutes a "public nuisance" under local law. SEE ALSO: OpenAI launches tool for finding child sexual abuse material Filed to the Superior Court of California on Monday , the lawsuit accuses OpenAI of violating California's unfair competition laws by engaging in "unlawful, unfair, or fraudulent acts or practices." Such alleged acts include making statements misleading people into believing OpenAI develops its AI models safely and responsibly, and testing said models without adequate security measures in place to protect the public. This lawsuit follows an incident in July where an OpenAI agent escaped its testing environment and hacked Hugging Face , an open-source repository of AI models, datasets, and tools. "The Hugging Face attack was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability and this was only one of 80 known incidents," California Attorney General Rob Bonta said in a press release. The filing cited several of these incidents, including a breach in June where an OpenAI agent hacked the Australian government's healthcare system . Researchers have previously identified multiple instances of AI models escaping and hacking external organisations, including some created by OpenAI. title: Three small failures combined to take down Microsoft 365
author: Nick Indge
body: A hidden defect in Microsoft's cloud gateway, dormant since July, was to blame for one of the largest outages in the company's history last week. A preliminary Post-Incident Report (PIR) released by the company outlines how the latent bug, changes in traffic, and reduced server capacity combined to knock much of Microsoft 365 and Exchange infrastructure offline at the end of last week. Microsoft's report lists the incident's final status as "a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents." Microsoft's preliminary report places the outage between November 12 at 16:20 UTC and November 13 at 16:10 UTC, just under 24 hours total, and additional monitoring remained in place for any affected systems through November 14. The outage started on November 12 and quickly rippled through businesses and public offices that depend on Microsoft's cloud and email exchange infrastructure. The outage is covered in Microsoft's incident IDs EX1550543 and MO1550821. You need Microsoft 365 admin credentials to see the full report on the company's status pages, but Office Watch has reproduced the preliminary report , and the University of Pennsylvania maintains an archive of Microsoft's service-health updates . title: OpenAI launches tool for finding child sexual abuse material
body: OpenAI announced Monday the release of a new tool to detect child sexual abuse material (CSAM), including content generated by artificial intelligence . The tool is a classifier that looks for visual signs of abuse in images. It then scores images to help human reviewers prioritize which of them warrant attention. OpenAI said its CSAM classifier is the first broadly available tool of its kind to include a specific signal indicating the image may be generated with AI. This capability is becoming critical as AI-generated CSAM skyrockets. A new analysis conducted by Childlight Global Child Safety Institute at the University of Edinburgh found AI-related reports of CSAM increased globally by more than 8,400 percent from 2023 to 2025. Last year, the National Center for Missing Exploited Children received more than 400,000 of these reports. In 2023, that number was roughly 4,700. SEE ALSO: How AI child sexual abuse material is colliding with free speech protections "Individual companies like OpenAI have a responsibility to prevent our technology from being exploited by predators to harm children, and we also must work together with the broader industry, child safety organizations and law enforcement to advance our collective efforts to protect children online," OpenAI said in its blog post about the announcement. The company's new tool can be used by organizations required or authorized to detect CSAM, including certain developers that use OpenAI's application programming interface, or API. title: How long it takes to play GTA 6: Playthrough and achievements
body: Grand Theft Auto VI is almost here. The highly anticipated video game will finally come out in the U.S. on Nov. 19, more than 13 years after its predecessor. SEE ALSO: 'GTA 6': 3 intriguing new details we just learned If you patiently waited more than a decade for GTA 6, you're probably hoping for a long, immersive experience that makes it worth the wait. Good news! Reports are now coming in from game reviewers, and it seems like you're in for a treat. You'll likely be playing GTA 6 for a long time. According to Insider Gaming , GTA 6 will take around 50 hours to complete the main campaign. That estimate covers nearly 100 missions across the five chapters of the game. Of course, your playtime may vary depending on your skill level. But, that seems to be the average based on reports. However, that's just the amount of time to complete GTA 6's main campaign. If you want to fully complete everything in the game, you're looking at a much longer gameplay time. Much longer. Aside from GTA 6's main campaign, there are also side quests and an array of interactions, events, and locations to explore. Gamers will likely want to unlock the reported 55 achievements, including the Platinum Trophy and the Mythic achievement. If you want to do all of that, you're looking at a reported 200 hours of gameplay for GTA 6. That's not even counting any time spent just wandering the streets of Vice City or cruising around in a car while listening to the stacked GTA 6 soundtrack . So, lock in, gamers (and please take plenty of breaks). More than 200 hours of GTA 6 await.

title: Hyperscale data centers use 2% of US electricity
author: Scott K. Johnson
body: One flashpoint for the tech industry’s all-in push on large language models has been the sudden rush to turn investment money into hyperscale data centers. The rush hasn’t allowed anyone to plan how to supply the required electricity cleanly or with minimal impact on ratepayers. Instead, it has been difficult to even collect information on what’s being built. A new study has tallied energy use and estimated emissions for hyperscalers operating in the United States between May 2024 and April 2025. They weren’t able to differentiate between AI compute and more traditional data services, but it provides a clear point of reference to track moving forward. Finding the centers The team started with a list of 675 facilities from a commercial database based on news reports, company statements, and satellite imagery. They dropped any that didn’t have a reported electrical capacity or that they couldn’t verify was a suitably large building with the expected cooling and electrical connection equipment. That reduced the list to 403 data centers with an average electrical capacity of about 40 megawatts. Read full article Comments

Namely, it is now rapidly moving toward rapidly reusable launch. However, it raises other questions. For example, as Starship becomes fully reusable, when might humans fly on the vehicle? title: What is vibe manufacturing? AI projects are leaving the chat
body: The next wave of AI projects might just arrive in the mail. As AI tools become more capable, people are asking chatbots to help design things they can hold, wear, or install in their homes, from custom jewelry and household gadgets to metal parts built around precise measurements. Welcome to " vibe manufacturing ." The phrase borrows from " vibe coding ," where people describe the software they want and ask AI to help create it. Here, the goal is a physical object, with AI helping develop a design that can be printed at home or sent to a manufacturer. The appeal is easy to understand. Most people have encountered a product that would be perfect if it were a little smaller, worked differently, or fit that one awkward space. These tools offer a starting point for making their own version. Getting it right, though, still takes more than a good prompt. SEE ALSO: What is vibe coding? Plus 7 AI coding tools to get started right away. What is vibe manufacturing? Vibe manufacturing loosely describes using conversational AI to help design and build physical things. Someone explains what they want, supplies measurements or reference images, and works with an AI tool to develop it. Depending on the project, that could involve generating a digital model, choosing components, writing software for a device, or figuring out assembly. The bridge between the conversation and the object is often CAD, short for computer-aided design . title: Microsoft outage cause revealed: It was a perfect storm of problems
body: You're probably aware that Microsoft 365, the popular suite of products that includes Outlook, suffered a massive global outage last week. In fact, it was the worst outage of the year , by a sizable margin. The problem took the computer giant roughly 24 hours, over the course of two business days , to get everything back up and running. Aside from wondering when their email would be working again , the number one question on everyone's mind was what in the world happened to keep Microsoft 365 down for so long? Now, we know. In a statement shared with customers and on X, Microsoft explained there were actually three causes, which created a perfect storm. First, a bug caused servers to become unresponsive in specific conditions; second, an issue with Microsoft Teams increased server traffic and created those conditions; and third, many additional servers were already offline from an unrelated issue. As Microsoft explained, on their own, neither issue would have caused such a large-scale problem. However, together, well, they kept one of the world's biggest tech companies scrambling for two days to fix their service. title: US now "comfortable" with children dying of measles as death toll hits 10
author: Beth Mole
body: Health officials in Pennsylvania and Wisconsin announced two more measles deaths late last week, bringing the national tally of confirmed measles deaths this year to 10. The total includes the deaths of at least four infants: two in Pennsylvania , one in New York , and one in Wisconsin . Wisconsin health officials said the latest measles death—the second for the state—was in a child. Pennsylvania's health department did not reveal the age or other details of the latest death—the state's seventh—besides revealing it was of an unvaccinated resident in Montour County. Overall, the seven deaths in Pennsylvania include two in Jefferson County, three in Lancaster County, and one in Mifflin, in addition to the new death in Montour. An eighth death was reported in Franklin County , but state health officials have not confirmed it. For all the states with deaths so far, health officials have noted that they're the first deaths in decades. Multiple outbreaks are underway across the country, pushing the national tally of cases to nearly 5,500 across 47 states and jurisdictions, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Pennsylvania's case count alone is over 1,500, and Wisconsin is reporting nearly 650. Read full article Comments

title: Its official: Robert Pattinson is our new James Bond
body: Martinis are flowing from the chimneys at Pinewood Studios, which can only mean one thing: We have our new James Bond. On Nov. 16, Amazon MGM Studios announced that the newest 007 will be Robert Pattinson. He takes over the role from Daniel Craig, whose last film was 2021's No Time to Die . The next Bond film, the franchise's 26th, will be helmed by Dune director Denis Villeneuve. Pattinson has also worked with Villeneuve on Dune: Part Three . View this post on Instagram Aside from the Bond announcement, 2026 has been a banner year for Pattinson. He topped the box office with The Odyssey and cemented himself as an A24 darling with roles in The Drama and Primetime . While Pattinson has starred in smaller, stranger indie projects, he has also developed a seemingly paradoxical reputation as a franchise man. He is Batman, after all, with The Batman: Part II set for a Feb. 18, 2028 release. Before Pattinson became Battinson, moody eyeshadow and all, he captured hearts as Edward Cullen in the Twilight franchise, as well as Cedric Diggory in Harry Potter . Plus, while not part of a franchise, his role as agent Neil in Christopher Nolan's Tenet proved he's got the chops to play a suave agent. Other contenders for film's most famous spy included Slow Horses ' Jack Lowden, One Night Only 's Callum Turner, Challengers ' Josh O'Connor, and Superman 's Nicholas Hoult, all of whom reportedly screen tested for the role. Frankenstein 's Jacob Elordi and Sinners ' Jack O'Connell were reportedly in the running as well, although did not end up screen testing.

title: Mercedes' clever new driving assist handles complex traffic like a champ
author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
body: Mercedes-Benz provided flights from Washington, DC, to San Francisco and accommodation so Ars could try its new driver assistance systems. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. SAN FRANCISCO—When Ars first drove the new Mercedes-Benz CLA last year , the automaker also gave us a sneak preview of its next driver assist. Called Drive Assist Pro, it’s for collaborative partially assisted driving, and from the passenger seat at the time, the demo was impressive . Now the automaker is getting ready to start rolling out Drive Assist Pro to customers with cars running the new MB.OS operating system here in the US and in Germany, and it let us have some time behind the wheel. While most automakers want a reputation for safety, Mercedes has long used passive and active technology to do so in its products. It was one of the first OEMs to introduce airbags, and a decade later started adding active safety systems like anti-lock brakes, electronic stability control, and adaptive cruise control. And so, by giving the car’s electronics the ability to control the brakes and throttle, we arrive at the first level of assisted driving—called “level 1” in automotive engineer-speak. “Level 2” assisted driving, where the car also controls the steering as well as the acceleration and braking, got famous with Tesla Autopilot. But the first lane-keeping assists predate it by almost a decade in passenger cars, when Toyota introduced a system in 2004. Developed by Kaleb Lechowski aka byKaleb, Drawquarium is a sweet new cozy sandbox game out on Steam that's essentially the bloomscrolling of video games. The premise of Drawquarium is simple: draw a fish, name it, and watch it come to life swimming in your own digital aquarium.
